# Leakage audit

<!-- Generated by `python -m scripts.audit.leakage_audit`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every number on this page is read from `reports/leakage_audit_*.json` and `reports/single_feature_auc_*.csv`, written by `scripts/audit/leakage_audit.py`.

Protocol: exact duplicate rows removed before the split; 80/20 stratified split (`random_state=42`); 5-fold stratified CV on the train part; one fixed `LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=42)` for every row, no tuning. The test part is only scored, never used to choose anything.

## IBM Telco

`data/raw/Telco_customer_churn.xlsx`: 7043 rows, 0 duplicates removed, train 5634 / test 1409, churn rate 26.5%. Always dropped (identifiers, and `Churn Label`, a copy of the target): `CustomerID`, `Count`, `Country`, `State`, `City`, `Zip Code`, `Lat Long`, `Latitude`, `Longitude`, `Churn Label`.

### (a) Leakage ladder

Each step fixes one more problem than the step above. *Reported* is the number the old system would show: for S0 it is max(CV AUC, AUC on the validation split after calibrating on that same split); from S1 on it is the CV AUC.

| Step | Change | CV AUC (mean ± std) | Calibrated val AUC | Reported | Test AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | As the old code: Churn Score/CLTV/Churn Reason kept; FE columns chosen on all rows; SMOTENC on the whole train part before CV; score = max(CV AUC, AUC on a val split after isotonic calibration on that same split) | 1.000 ± 0.000 | 1.000 | **1.000** | 1.000 |
| S1 | Report CV AUC only (no max with calibrated val AUC) | 1.000 ± 0.000 | — | **1.000** | 1.000 |
| S2 | SMOTENC inside the imblearn Pipeline (fit per fold) | 1.000 ± 0.000 | — | **1.000** | 1.000 |
| S3 | Generic FE column choice fitted on the training fold (in Pipeline) | 1.000 ± 0.000 | — | **1.000** | 1.000 |
| S4 | Drop Churn Reason | 0.982 ± 0.002 | — | **0.982** | 0.980 |
| S5 | Drop Churn Score and CLTV | 0.849 ± 0.014 | — | **0.849** | 0.841 |
| S6 | No SMOTE; LightGBM class_weight='balanced' | 0.848 ± 0.014 | — | **0.848** | 0.841 |

### What the numbers say

- The old protocol reports **1.000** on this file; the clean setup (S6) scores **0.841** on the untouched test set.
- Gap between CV AUC and test AUC per step (positive = CV is optimistic): S0 +0.000, S1 +0.000, S2 +0.000, S3 +0.000, S4 +0.002, S5 +0.008, S6 +0.008.
- `Churn Reason` is missing for 100.0% of non-churners and 0.0% of churners in the training split: its missingness alone separates the classes (missing-indicator AUC 0.000, i.e. 1.000 inverted). It only exists after a customer has left.
- `Churn Score` alone reaches CV AUC 0.940. Per IBM's column description, `Churn Score` and `CLTV` are outputs of IBM's own models, not raw customer attributes.
- `Churn Reason` makes every model perfect, which hides the SMOTE effect in the ladder. With clean features, SMOTENC before CV gives CV AUC 0.928 vs 0.849 when it is fitted per fold, while test AUC is 0.841 vs 0.841: the oversampling leak inflates the CV estimate, not the model.
- Clean LightGBM minus Logistic Regression on test ROC-AUC: -0.008 (95% CI [-0.019, 0.003]). The interval contains 0: no evidence that LightGBM beats the linear baseline on this file.
- Generic FE columns chosen on all rows (S2): `Churn Score`, `Tenure Months`, `Total Charges`, `Monthly Charges`, `CLTV`; chosen on the train part (S3): `Churn Score`, `Tenure Months`, `Monthly Charges`, `Total Charges`, `CLTV`. The selection is identical, so S2 → S3 isolates no leakage on this file.

### Stop check

Rule: stop if single-feature AUC of Status, Customer Value > 0.9 or clean LightGBM test AUC > 0.97.

- `Status` alone: 0.788
- `Customer Value` alone: 0.759
- Clean LightGBM test AUC: 0.990
- Triggered: **yes — needs a decision before any column is called leakage**

### Where the high AUC comes from (training split only)

All 13 columns: CV AUC 0.985.

| Dropped column | CV AUC | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `Complains` | 0.980 | -0.005 |
| `Subscription  Length` | 0.980 | -0.004 |
| `Call  Failure` | 0.981 | -0.004 |
| `Seconds of Use` | 0.981 | -0.004 |
| `Status` | 0.981 | -0.003 |
| `Frequency of use` | 0.982 | -0.003 |
| `Tariff Plan` | 0.985 | -0.000 |
| `Age Group` | 0.985 | +0.000 |
| `Age` | 0.985 | +0.000 |
| `Charge  Amount` | 0.985 | +0.000 |
| `Customer Value` | 0.985 | +0.001 |
| `Distinct Called Numbers` | 0.985 | +0.001 |
| `Frequency of SMS` | 0.986 | +0.002 |
| `Status` + `Customer Value` | 0.982 | -0.002 |

Best two-column models (shallow LightGBM): `Complains` + `Frequency of use` 0.898; `Complains` + `Seconds of Use` 0.895; `Seconds of Use` + `Frequency of use` 0.882; `Seconds of Use` + `Status` 0.881; `Complains` + `Customer Value` 0.880.

`Customer Value` predicted from the other 12 columns: CV R² 0.979 (linear), 0.996 (LightGBM).

- Churn rate by `Status`: 1 → 5.7% (n=1734), 2 → 47.4% (n=546).
- Churn rate by `Complains`: 0 → 10.0% (n=2098), 1 → 81.3% (n=182).

**Reading.** The best single column reaches 0.789 (`Seconds of Use`) and the best pair 0.898; removing any one column moves CV AUC by at most 0.005 (largest drop: `Complains`). The score comes from many usage columns together, not from one column that encodes the label. `Customer Value` is close to a function of the other columns, so it is redundant rather than a separate leak. Per the UCI description all columns are aggregated over months 1–9 and the label is taken at month 12. Decision (2026-10-14): no column is treated as leakage; all 13 are kept, and the AUC is reported as unusually high for a churn problem. The source does not document why this file is so separable.
